problem: In the forest, there live 40 animals - foxes, wolves, hares, and badgers. Every year they organize a masquerade ball: each one wears a mask of another animal type, and they do not wear the same mask for two consecutive years. Two years ago, at the ball, there were 12 "foxes" and 28 "wolves", last year there were 15 "hares", 10 "foxes", and 15 "badgers", and this year there are 15 "hares" and 25 "foxes". Which animals are the most numerous in the forest?

answer_text:
Looking at this problem, I need to track mask assignments across three years for 40 animals of four types (foxes F, wolves W, hares H, badgers B), where each animal wears a mask of a **different** type and never repeats a mask in consecutive years.

## Setting Up the Constraints

**Two years ago:** 12 fox-masks, 28 wolf-masks (no hare/badger masks)
- Foxes MUST wear wolf masks (only option), so all $f$ foxes → wolf masks
- Wolves MUST wear fox masks (only option), so all $w$ wolves → fox masks

**Last year:** 10 fox-masks, 15 hare-masks, 15 badger-masks (no wolf masks)

**This year:** 25 fox-masks, 15 hare-masks (no wolf/badger masks)
- Foxes MUST wear hare masks (only option): all $f$ foxes → hare masks
- Hares MUST wear fox masks (only option): all $h$ hares → fox masks

## Applying Consecutive-Year (No-Repeat) Constraints
